The procedure must be named sp and accept four parameters in this exact order: para_Age as NUMBER, para_Name as VARCHAR2, para_Party as VARCHAR2, and para_Home_city as VARCHAR2. Because the cursor selects the entire driver row, it reads driver.Driver_ID, driver.Name, driver.Party, driver.Home_city, and driver.Age. It writes driver.Name and driver.Home_city. It deletes rows from driver based on driver.Party. It reads school_bus.Driver_ID and school_bus.Years_Working, and it writes school_bus.Years_Working. The number 1 is used as the increment, and the null literal is used to test driver.Party.

Operations must occur in the following order.

First, open a cursor over the driver rows where driver.Age is strictly greater than para_Age and driver.Party is equal to para_Party. Both conditions must be true for a row to be included. The cursor locks the selected driver rows for update.

Then loop through the cursor one row at a time. For each fetched row, set driver.Name to para_Name. If the cursor finds no rows that satisfy both conditions, the loop does not run and no driver.Name values are changed by this part.

After the loop finishes, close the cursor.

Next, delete every row from the driver table whose driver.Party is null. If there are no such rows, no deletion occurs.

Next, update every remaining row in the driver table by setting driver.Home_city to para_Home_city. This applies to all driver rows present at that point. If there are no driver rows, this step has no effect.

Finally, update the school_bus table by increasing school_bus.Years_Working by 1 for every school_bus row whose school_bus.Driver_ID matches the driver.Driver_ID of any driver row whose driver.Party is equal to para_Party at that moment. If no driver rows have a driver.Party equal to para_Party, or if no school_bus row has a matching school_bus.Driver_ID, no school_bus rows are updated.

The procedure has no explicit exception handling. Any error raised during opening, fetching, updating, or deleting is not caught inside the procedure and propagates to the caller. The procedure also does not issue an explicit commit or rollback.
